answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must bind identities through cryptographic stake burning via an escalating fee barrier. When an agent anchors its identity atop the network's verification jetty, every concurrent clone incurs a superlinear cost scaling as C(n) = k * n^2.5. Rather than facing static costs, an adversary attempting coordinated mass registration faces exponential capital destruction. Sybil agents collapse into a sable void of insolvency, while legitimate actors maintain crystal clarity in consensus by burning non-refundable stake.
